Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1225 AM CDT Sat Aug 01 2026

Valid 021200Z - 031200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM THE UPPER
OHIO VALLEY INTO THE CAROLINAS AND PARTS OF GEORGIA...AND OVER A
PART OF THE NORTHERN PLAINS...

...SUMMARY...
Isolated occurrences of mainly damaging winds are possible from the
upper Ohio Valley into the Carolinas and parts of Georgia Sunday
afternoon and evening. A more conditional severe risk exists across
parts of North Dakota into far northwest Minnesota late Sunday
night.

...Synopsis...

A mid-level low initially over the lower OH Valley Sunday morning is
forecast to evolve into an open wave while slowly moving through the
OH and TN Valleys. That feature will be loosely linked to a
strengthening mid-level trough over eastern ON into QC. Elsewhere,
an intense upper low will move from AB into SK with an attending
belt of 50-70 kt winds at 500 mb spreading from the northern Rockies
into the northern High Plains. 

At the surface, an area of low pressure will move through the OH
Valley with a trailing wind shift/weak front moving across the TN
Valley and Gulf Coast states. There is also a signal for a diffuse
warm front to lift north through the Mid-Atlantic and southern New
England. Farther northwest, a cold front will advance into the
northern Plains.  


...Upper Ohio Valley into the Southeast...

Showers and thunderstorms are expected to be ongoing Sunday morning
from the lower Great Lakes into the central Appalachians within the
warm-conveyor air stream preceding the OH Valley low. The presence
of a moist and at least modestly unstable environment with little to
no capping will allow showers and storms to persist through the day
in some areas. Where cloud breaks can occur, increased daytime
heating will support corridors of MLCAPE up to 1000-1500 J/kg. 
 
More intense storms appear possible during the afternoon within the
areas of greater instability, from near and east of the surface low
in the upper OH Valley south along and ahead of the front into GA.
The strongest deep-layer shear of 30-35 kt is forecast near the
surface low, where some storm organization appears possible, given
sufficient destabilization. Another area of potential interest is
along the diffuse warm front, which is forecast to lift through the
southern Mid-Atlantic during the late afternoon into evening. While
deep-layer shear will be somewhat limited, locally backed surface
winds combined with a broadening and strengthening low-level jet may
enhance low-level shear in the vicinity of the boundary. 

Locally damaging wind gusts appear to be the primary hazard with the
most intense storms during the afternoon into evening. However, a
brief tornado cannot be ruled out near the warm front. The
probability of that occurrence currently appears to be less than 2%.
 

...Northern Plains...

While boundary-layer moisture content will remain somewhat limited,
the presence of steep low/mid-level lapse rates is expected to yield
an axis of moderate instability ahead the front with MLCAPE of
1000-1500 J/kg. Despite pre-frontal temperatures warming into the
90s to around 100, afternoon storm development remains uncertain due
to capping at the base of an EML and the absence of forcing for
ascent. Some of the 00Z models indicate a greater possibility of
isolated storm development (mainly elevated) late Sunday night as
the cap is gradually eroded by increasing height falls aloft.
Strengthening vertical shear combined with steep mid-level lapse
rates and MUCAPE of 1000-2000 J/kg suggests a conditional risk for
severe storms capable of large hail and perhaps locally damaging
wind gusts. The level 1/Marginal Risk will be maintained due to
uncertainties in storm development and potential coverage.

..Mead.. 08/01/2026

$$

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0225 AM CDT Sat Aug 01 2026

Valid 031200Z - 041200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER EASTERN NORTH
DAKOTA...NORTHWEST MINNESOTA...AND A SMALL PART OF NORTHEAST SOUTH
DAKOTA...

...SUMMARY...
Widely scattered to scattered severe storms appear possible in
eastern North Dakota, northwest Minnesota, and a small part of
northeast South Dakota Monday afternoon and evening. Severe wind
gusts and large hail will be the primary hazards. More isolated
occurrences of mainly damaging wind are possible from central and
eastern South Dakota into western Nebraska, and in portions of the
Mid-Atlantic into southern New England.

...Synopsis...

A vigorous short-wave trough and attending mid/upper-level jet
streaks initially over the northern Rockies Monday morning will
progress through the northern Plains and the upper MS Valley. At the
surface, an area of low pressure is expected to develop from western
SD into northern MN, along a cold front advancing through the
northern Plains and upper MS Valley. The southern extension of the
front will push into the central High Plains.

Elsewhere, a short-wave trough will progress through northern New
England within the base of a trough situated over QC. That mid-level
system will be associated with a surface front that will move
through the Northeast.


...Northern and central Plains into the upper Mississippi Valley...

Thunderstorms may be ongoing at 12Z Monday across portions of ND
within the leading edge of height falls preceding the mid-level
trough. In the wake of the early-day storms, steep lapse rates and a
relatively moist boundary layer will combine with daytime heating to
yield a moderately unstable but capped air mass by afternoon ahead
of the cold front. Renewed thunderstorm development is anticipated
at that time along the cold front across eastern ND into northwest
MN, where stronger dynamic forcing for ascent should erode the cap.
There, forecast soundings indicate vertically veering wind profiles
with steadily strengthening low-level and deep-layer shear,
supportive of supercells and bowing structures capable of mainly
large hail and damaging winds. Potentially larger
temperature-dewpoint spreads and resultant higher LCL heights may
curb the tornado threat to some extent.

Storm development farther south along the front in SD and NE remains
more uncertain due to capping concerns. Should storms develop, the
environment would support the potential for isolated occurrences of
severe wind gusts and perhaps some large hail.


...Southern New England into the Mid-Atlantic...

The potential for early-day storms leads to uncertainty in the
degree of air mass destabilization by afternoon along and ahead of
the front moving south through the region. However, where stronger
heating can occur, the presence of a moist air mass will support
pockets of moderate instability by afternoon. Forcing within the
right entrance region of an upper-level jet streak lifting through
northern New England will combine with the front to yield an
increase in storms through the afternoon within a kinematic
environment featuring 30-35 kt of deep-layer shear. As such, a few
strong to severe storms appear possible, with the primary hazard
being damaging wind gusts.

..Mead.. 08/01/2026

$$

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0317 AM CDT Sat Aug 01 2026

Valid 041200Z - 091200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Day 4/Tuesday...

A broader-scale trough is forecast over central Canada into the
north-central U.S. with a series of subtle disturbances moving
through the base of that feature. At the surface, a front is
expected to move through the upper Great Lakes with the western
extension of the boundary settling slowly south through the central
High Plains. A severe weather threat may materialize from the mid MO
Valley into the central High Plains along the front and in the
post-frontal upslope, where an overlap of moderate instability and
stronger vertical shear is expected to reside.

Elsewhere, a more widespread area of moderate instability developing
across southern AZ could support a locally greater risk of severe
storms. 

The extent of the severe weather threat in both areas is currently
too uncertain to delineate an area. 
 

...Day 5/Wednesday...

The broad, cyclonic flow regime will continue over the north-central
CONUS with a belt of slightly enhanced mid-level winds extending
from the northern Rockies through the northern and central Plains
into the Great Lakes. At the surface, the previously mentioned front
will continue through the Great Lakes with the boundary extending
southwest through the mid MS Valley into the central or southern
High Plains. Similar to Day 4/Tuesday, some severe weather appears
possible along the boundary over the lower MO into mid MS Valleys,
as well as within the post-frontal upslope across the central High
Plains. 

The subtle nature of the forcing for ascent leads to uncertainty in
severe storm coverage, so no area will be included. 


...Days 6-8/Thursday through Saturday...

The 00Z ensemble means are in reasonably good agreement in depicting
the continuation of an upper high over the southwestern U.S. with
lower-amplitude troughing over the Great Lakes into the Northeast.
At the surface, there is considerable model spread in the location
of relevant boundaries that might focus severe storms. That being
said, much of the available AI guidance suggests an increasing
severe weather threat in the Mid-Atlantic during this time frame. 

Model trends will continue to be monitored for the possible
inclusion of an area in subsequent outlooks.

..Mead.. 08/01/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1116 AM CDT Sat Aug 01 2026

Valid 011630Z - 021200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE OHIO AND TENNESSEE VALLEYS...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe wind gusts and an isolated tornado threat
are expected across parts of the Ohio and Tennessee Valleys this
afternoon into evening. Isolated severe wind gusts will also be
possible in parts of New Mexico, southeast Arizona, and Far West
Texas.

..OH and TN Valleys...
Recent satellite imagery shows a positively tilted shortwave trough
moving through the Mid MS Valley. Surface analysis shows an occluded
surface low over central IL beneath the shortwave. Expectation is
for this cyclone to drift slowly east-southeastward throughout the
day, with the surface low gradually filling. As this low fills, the
triple point low, currently near the IL/IN/KY border intersection,
will become more prominent through the afternoon before it too
occludes.

Showers and thunderstorms are currently ongoing from eastern
IN/western OH through eastern TN into AL, along the eastern
periphery of an arcing warm conveyor. These showers and
thunderstorms should continue northeastward/eastward as the entire
system drifts east-southeastward, with some modest moisture
advection anticipated throughout the warm sector. This should allow
the warm sector to at least moderately destabilize, but persistent
cloudiness will limit heating, likely tempering the overall
buoyancy. Expectation is for more modest buoyancy (i.e. MLCAPE
around 500 to 1000 J/kg) across IN and OH, with greater buoyancy
(i.e. MLCAPE around 1500 J/kg) farther south across central KY and
Middle TN. Thunderstorm development is anticipated along and ahead
of the cold front as it moves through this destabilized and buoyant
airmass.

Moderate mid-level flow throughout the base of the Mid MS Valley
shortwave trough will spread eastward across KY and TN, supporting
effective shear around 30 to 35 kt across KY. Reduced vertical shear
is expected farther north across the OH Valley (due to weaker
mid-level flow) and farther south across TN Valley (due to more
westerly low-level flow). Given these kinematic conditions, a
predominantly multicellular mode is favored, although a few
supercells appear possible from southeast IN/southwest OH through
central KY. Damaging wind gusts will be the most prominent hazard,
but a tornado or two is also possible, particularly within the
corridor from far southeast IN through far north-central KY and far
southwest OH. Here, some modestly increased low-level shear is
possible near the triple point low as it moves through.

...Eastern AZ through NM into west TX...
Moderate mid-level moisture will support afternoon thunderstorm
development across the higher terrain from western AZ through
central/northeast NM. Relatively strong northerly winds aloft will
aid storm organization/clustering as storms spread
south-southeastward into the deeply mixed boundary-layer across the
lower elevations. Outflow-dominant storm structures will result in
strong cold pools capable of isolated strong to severe wind gusts.
Resulting forward-propagating lines could reach as far
south/southeast as Far West TX by later this evening.

..Mosier/Lyons.. 08/01/2026
